summary: The agent implemented nearly all inherited-super-mapping behavior and passed all 3,649 baseline tests plus 101 of 103 new tests, but its override discovery only accepts abstract super methods, so mappings on an overridden interface default method are rejected as if no mapping method were overridden.
quick_failure_summary: Overridden default mapping methods are not recognized for super-mapping inheritance.

details.reasoning: In MethodRetrievalProcessor, collectOverriddenMappingMethods requires candidate.getModifiers().contains(Modifier.ABSTRACT) before calling elementUtils.overrides. A Java interface default mapping method can be overridden and can carry @Mapping declarations, but this filter excludes it. Consequently both compiler variants of overriddenDefaultMethodMappingsAreInherited fail with the agent's own no-super-method diagnostic. The implementation is otherwise substantial and the remaining hidden cases pass, so this is a completed solution with one explicit requirement omitted rather than early termination or a broad algorithmic failure.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's focused regression suite covered abstract interface methods, generic/transitive inheritance, diamonds, compositions, rebinding, conflicts, flattening, configuration precedence, and empty parents, but did not include a concrete/default overridden mapping method; its final validation therefore missed the restrictive ABSTRACT filter.

justification.issue_description: Override discovery excludes non-abstract overridden mapping methods, specifically interface default methods with property mappings.
justification.evidence: The prompt says the option applies when a bean-mapping method 'overrides mapper interface or superclass methods' and imposes no abstract-only restriction. Java default interface methods are overridable methods, and the visible processor utility delegates to Elements.overrides without requiring ABSTRACT. The agent nevertheless added candidate.getModifiers().contains(Modifier.ABSTRACT), while the hidden DefaultMethodParentK7p4 declares @Mapping on a default map method and both resulting tests fail with '@BeanMapping#inheritSuperMappings is enabled, but this method does not override a mapping method.'
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than an undocumented edge case or test mismatch because the task deliberately uses the general Java override relationship across mapper interfaces and superclasses. A competent implementation should not add an abstract-only restriction absent from the prompt, particularly when Elements.overrides already supplies the intended semantic test.

problem_assessment.notes: The prompt is detailed about precedence, conflicts, flattening, generic/transitive supertypes, source rebinding, expressions, empty overridden mappings, and interaction with existing inheritance. The default-method case is a fair instance of the stated unrestricted override behavior. The reference solution demonstrates feasibility, and the hidden suite deterministically isolates the missing case across two compiler modes.

evidence: JUnit reports 3,649/3,649 baseline tests passing and 101/103 new tests passing, so the runtime and test bootstrap exercised the implementation normally.

Both failures have the same feature-specific compilation diagnostic emitted by agent-modified MethodRetrievalProcessor for DefaultMethodMapperK7p4, rather than a dependency, import, permission, or shared setup crash.
The trajectory shows successful compilation, focused tests on javac and Eclipse, and a successful reactor verification; no external failure prevented implementation or validation.

The post-agent harness logged an initial three-way test.patch merge failure but recovered by resetting patch files, reapplying the patch, and executing all 103 new tests, so it did not block or invalidate grading.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the two verifier failures are directly explained by the implementation's abstract-only override filter.
